$comment: Skill frontmatter keys each host documents, read from the host's own documentation. validate_frontmatter fails when a skill or command schema declares one of these keys as a package-owned key - a key the package gives its own meaning - because the host reads the key first and the package's meaning is lost (road-to-skills-that-arrive-when-called 1.2; the defect it guards is `context: large`, renamed to `context_window` in 1.1). A key the package declares WITH the host's meaning is listed under `passthrough` with the reason. A host entry past `expires` is reported as a warning: re-read the page, update `keys` and `read_date`, and move `expires` forward.

passthrough.name: The skill or command slug; the host reads it as the invocation name, which is the package's meaning.
passthrough.description: The trigger line; the host lists it, which is the package's meaning.
passthrough.effort: Declared as a verbatim passthrough to the host's effort knob (skill schema description).
passthrough.user-invocable: Declared as the host's own extension, used to keep a built-in name unshadowed.
passthrough.compatibility: Declared as the Agent Skills spec field with the spec's meaning; deprecated in the skill schema.
passthrough.argument-hint: Commands project as host skills; the hint is the host's argument hint.
passthrough.disable-model-invocation: Commands project as host skills; the flag is the host's own.
